source_title: Joshimath Chopper Crash: Search On For Missing Trans Bharat Flight - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
A helicopter carrying six individuals, including five passengers and a pilot, went missing and crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district. The aircraft, operated by Trans Bharat Aviation, departed from Badrinath at 1:14 p.m. bound for Sahastradhara heliport in Dehradun before communication was lost while traversing the Joshimath valley. Following the incident, the Chamoli district administration, the State Disaster Response Force, and an Indian Army unit were deployed to the suspected crash site to conduct search and rescue operations. As a precautionary measure, the entire fleet of Trans Bharat Aviation helicopters has been grounded. Adverse weather conditions in the mountainous terrain have created severe hurdles for emergency rescue personnel attempting to access the site. An investigation into the exact cause of the crash will follow the ongoing search and rescue efforts. Read More

Diljit Dosanjh Made To Fill C-Form At Agra Hotel Under FRRO Foreign Rules
Actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh was required to fill out a mandatory C-form under Foreigners Regional Registration Office regulations during his stay at a five-star hotel in Agra. Indian rules mandate that any foreign national staying at a hotel, homestay, or guest house must complete this digital document, allowing the government to track foreign visitors. The hotel informed the authorities after Dosanjh's team initially refused to fill the form, citing that he had never completed one during previous stays in India. Following a warning from the Lucknow registration office team that non-compliance could result in legal action or an FIR, the singer completed the document.

Markets End Above 23,000, IT Leads Rally, CCS Clears ₹40,000 Cr Stealth Corvettes
Indian benchmark equity indices closed higher on Friday, with the Nifty closing above 23,000 and the Sensex trading near 74,500 despite crude oil prices crossing 118 dollars a barrel. IT and pharma stocks led the gains, while mid and small caps faced selling pressure. Other major domestic developments included the Cabinet Committee on Security clearing an over 40,000 crore rupee project for eight next-generation stealth corvettes to be constructed by GRSE and Goa Shipyard Limited with more than 70 percent indigenous content. Additionally, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman defended the IDBI Bank stake sale, highlighting previous recapitalization efforts, and Walmart initiated an internal investigation into alleged kickbacks at Flipkart. Market experts discussed corporate earnings, rising crude prices, aviation challenges faced by IndiGo, and investment outlooks for Samvat 2083 across equities, fixed income, and gold.
Congress Has 'Anarchic Model' in Power and Opposition: Sudhanshu Trivedi
Bharatiya Janata Party MP Dr. Sudhanshu Trivedi mounted an attack against the Congress party, accusing it of having an 'anarchic model' both in governance and opposition. Trivedi questioned the Congress over its track record in states it governs, challenging the party to showcase its development models. Comparing this with the governance of BJP-led states and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's tenure as Chief Minister of Gujarat, Trivedi cited initiatives like groundwater revival, interest-free loans for farmers, and law enforcement reforms. He also alleged internal factionalism within Congress state units, citing past rifts in Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, and Karnataka, while questioning the party's overseas engagements.
